articles.dek: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of…
articles.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. articles.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
articles.dek: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to…
articles.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

articles.dek: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and…
articles.description: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil . Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club.
